newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Treacherous S.Africa sea swallows Panama freighter.
newsitem.headline: Treacherous S.Africa sea swallows Panama freighter.

text.p: A freighter went down with all hands in heavy seas off the east coast of South Africa on Thursday. Rescuers said they had spotted five bodies of the 29-member crew, now all presumed lost.
The search for survivors of the wreck of the Panamanian-registered 12,000-tonne mixed-cargo ship Cordiglier was called off as light began to fade, with high seas and strong winds persisting.
"Our rescue teams have not found any survivors. So far they have only picked up three bodies from the sea," South African air force spokesman Roy Bridge told Reuters.
Durban port captain Ron Holloway said two other bodies had been sighted before the search was called of at about 1300 GMT.
"The search has been called off and we assume all people who were on the ship have been killed," he told Reuters.
"We are busy organising that two more bodies be picked up by an NSRI (National Sea Rescue Institute) boat because the (two air force) helicopters are now on their way back."
The 155-metre freighter set off from the Indian Ocean port of Durban early on Wednesday.
The vessel ran into the rough seas and began taking on water about five nautical miles off Port St Johns on South Africa's Wild Coast at 0030 GMT on Thursday, Holloway said.
The Cordiglier had been en route to Cape Town and the West African cities of Lagos and Abidjan.
"The last report from the ship was: 'I am taking on water, I need assistance...'," Holloway added.
Bridge said two South African Navy divers had been among the rescuers but swells of up to four metres (14 feet) had made it impossible for them to scour the waters with the hope of finding survivors.
"Throughout the search the sea has been very bad and our reports show we had a strong south westerly of about 35 knots in the area," he said.
Patches of debris including three badly damaged life rafts, one capsized lifeboat as well as paper reels and a patch of oil were scattered over the area where the freigher went down.
South Africa's east coast stretch from around Port Edward up to Port Elizabeth is notorious for rough sea conditions, shipping authorities say.
Last month 16 men drowned when two local fishing trawlers capsized near Cape St Francis, and a number of vessels have also run aground recently.
